audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it outright: NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, sequencingCues 0. Not one number appeared in any string, so 'trade only from full courage' and 'this is his kill window' had nothing to time against.
audit.why: Alpha Strike is 20/19.5/19/18.5/18s and his basic attacks shorten it. Meditate is a flat 10s. Wuju Style is a flat 14s. Highlander is a flat 85s. Those four numbers are the whole rhythm of the lane.
audit.corrected: The 20s Alpha Strike, 14s Wuju Style, 10s Meditate and 85s Highlander written into whys[2] through whys[5] and the two mid-game spikes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions were absent. (a) Alpha Strike makes him untargetable — a Bear Trap or CHAAAARGE aimed at it simply whiffs. (b) Highlander makes him immune to ALL slowing effects, so Bear Trap's slow does nothing for its whole duration. (c) Meditate is a channel, so any CC cancels it — the Bear Trap yank interrupts his heal outright, and nothing on the page said so.
audit.why: These are the three moments the matchup actually turns on, and a reader trapping into Alpha Strike or expecting his slow to stick through Highlander loses the fight he thought he had won.
audit.corrected: Untargetability, slow-immunity and the Meditate interrupt written into whys[2], whys[4], spikes[1].text and spikes[2].text.

audit.why: Meditate restores health and reduces damage taken on a flat 10s, and it also banks Double Strike stacks while pausing Wuju Style and Highlander — in an extended trade it is his entire sustain engine, and Grievous Wounds is what blunts it.
